criteria.description: Correctly identifies the Laplace approximation as a Taylor expansion of the energy function at the mode.
Correctly explains why the linear term vanishes and why the result is Gaussian.

solutions.fullSolution: The energy E(x)=-log p(x)+c is Taylor-expanded to second order around its minimum x* (the mode of p). The linear term vanishes because x* is a critical point of E, gradient exactly zero. What remains is purely quadratic in (x-x*); exponentiating a quadratic gives a Gaussian's exponent form exactly.

criteria.description: Correctly explains D(q||p)>=0 makes the optimization well-posed (bounded below).
Correctly explains D(q*||p)=0 would mean q*=p exactly.

solutions.fullSolution: D(q||p)>=0 guarantees the objective has a known lower bound (zero), so the search is well-posed, not able to run to -infinity. If the family contains p itself, D=0 is achievable exactly when q=p (KL is zero iff the distributions are identical). In practice the family usually doesn't contain p, so D(q*||p)>0 at the optimum; the guarantee is only that the result is the closest achievable member of the family.

criteria.description: Correctly expands log p(x)-log q(x) and takes the expectation under p term by term.
Correctly arrives at the closed form and evaluates it numerically (~0.443).

solutions.fullSolution: log p(x)-log q(x) = log(sigma2/sigma1) - (x-mu1)^2/(2 sigma1^2) + (x-mu2)^2/(2 sigma2^2). Taking E_p: E_p{(x-mu1)^2}=sigma1^2, E_p{(x-mu2)^2}=sigma1^2+(mu1-mu2)^2. Result: D(p||q) = log(sigma2/sigma1) - 1/2 + (sigma1^2+(mu1-mu2)^2)/(2 sigma2^2). For mu1=0,s1=1,mu2=1,s2=2: log2 - 0.5 + 2/8 = log2-0.5+0.25 ~= 0.443. Independently verified via Monte Carlo estimation of the expectation.
log(1/1.5) + (2.25+4)/2 - 0.5 = -0.4055 + 3.125 - 0.5 = 2.2195. Independently verified via Monte Carlo estimation.
d/dx log p = -2x^3+2x, critical points 0,+-1. d2/dx2 = -6x^2+2; at x=1: -4<0 (mode). sigma^2 = (-(-4))^-1 = 0.25.
d/dx log p = -2x^3+4x, critical points 0,+-sqrt(2). d2/dx2 = -6x^2+4; at x=sqrt(2): -8<0 (mode). sigma^2 = (-(-8))^-1 = 0.125.
